_readme: Past events, newest first (the Seed to success feature is in main.html). Each makes a card on events.html and a post at event-<id>.html. 'when' is shown as written. 'mode' is offline or online. 'role' is our part in it. Photos: assets/events/<photo>.webp; the card photo is 3:2 unless fit is contain. In post text, [words](page.html) makes a link. After a change run: python tools/team/build.py. Written from the co-founders' LinkedIn posts ('source', not shown on the site); guests are not named. Dates they don't give: IFTA and GITEX from the organisers' coverage, BNI from the Grimaldi Forum listing, RRU from its poster. 'March 2026' and 'Early 2026' come from the posting dates (23 Mar and 7 Feb 2026). 'review' notes are for us and are never shown; the full list is docs/pre-launch-review.md.

past.title: BNI Global Convention
past.text: A stand to connect Indian companies in deep tech, defence, clean energy, fintech and pharma with global companies, family offices and advisors.
past.alt: Announcement: Your Gateway to India’s Emerging Opportunities, BNI 2026 Global Convention, Monaco

post.title: Taking Indian companies to Monaco
post.lede: For the BNI Global Convention in Monaco we had one purpose: to connect some of India’s most promising companies with the world, and the world with India.

p: India is far more than a market. It makes things, it invents things, and it is one of the strongest growth stories of this decade.

list: Global companies, family offices and advisors looking at India for investments, joint ventures or vendor partnerships.
Strategic partners who can help our companies in deep tech, defence, clean energy, fintech and pharma go global.

p: We exhibited on 28 and 29 October, and were in Monaco from 27 October to meet people before the expo opened.

post.close: Looking at India, or want to take an Indian company further?

past.title: FWD Supreme launch, Flying Wedge
past.text: Our portfolio company Flying Wedge Defence & Aerospace unveiled the full-scale static prototype of FWD Supreme, its AI-piloted fighter aircraft.
past.alt: Guests standing in a row in front of the FWD Supreme prototype

post.title: An AI-piloted fighter aircraft takes the stage
post.lede: On 13 October 2026 our portfolio company Flying Wedge Defence & Aerospace unveiled FWD Supreme in New Delhi: the full-scale static prototype of an AI-piloted, fighter-class aircraft.

p: Suhas Tejaskanda founded [Flying Wedge](portfolio-flying-wedge.html) in 2022. Four years later, an aircraft designed and engineered in India stood in front of the room.
FWD Supreme is not a remote-controlled drone. It is designed to fly and make decisions using AI, and to fight in a coordinated swarm, under what the company calls its Mobbing Doctrine.

Deep tech and defence companies are rarely built in a single round. They need conviction, patience and the right people around them. That is why we back founders who set out to build something nobody has built before.

post.close: Building something bold in deep tech?

A guest standing under the nose of the FWD Supreme prototype

past.title: Bihar StartUp Showcase
past.text: Sixteen shortlisted founders pitched one to one to early-stage investors at the second edition, hosted by CIMP-BIIF. Monica Gupta and Nimit Shah took part.
past.alt: Collage of moments from the second edition of the Bihar Startup Showcase

post.title: Sixteen founders in Patna
post.lede: Monica Gupta and Nimit Shah spent a day in Patna for the second edition of the Bihar StartUp Showcase, hosted by CIMP-BIIF at the CIMP campus.

p: Sixteen shortlisted start-ups met angel networks and venture capital investors for individual pitches and negotiations, alongside keynotes and panel discussions.
Much of the discussion was about what investors weigh once the deck is closed: evidence that the market wants the product, how risk is managed, and whether the business can scale.

We came away with a belief confirmed. Bihar’s start-up ecosystem is past the point of emerging, and it will not be long before the rest of the country notices. Our thanks to CIMP-BIIF for building the platform.

post.close: Building outside the big cities? We would like to hear from you.

past.title: The Startup Mixer
past.text: The first edition: a curated evening for founders, investors and advisors at Santé Spa Cuisine, with Global St. Angelo’s Venture Funding and Vis Legis Law Practice.
past.alt: The Startup Mixer poster: capital, connections and strategic growth

post.title: The Startup Mixer comes to BKC
post.lede: An evening in Mumbai where founders sit across the table from investors who can back them, advisors who have seen what works, and others building companies of their own.

p: We co-hosted the Mixer with Global St. Angelo’s Venture Funding and Vis Legis Law Practice at Santé Spa Cuisine, from 4 to 6 pm. Seats were limited and the guest list was curated, so the conversations had room to go somewhere.

list: Conversations about capital, with people ready to invest.
Connections that help with the next phase of growth.

p: The Mixer is recurring, and Edition 5 is set for 2 December 2026 at the same venue. Details, and later dates, are under [upcoming events](events.html#upcoming).

post.close: Great ideas, good advice and the right capital belong in one room.

past.review: Details and photos of Editions 2 to 4 to come. Event photos of Edition 1 wanted.

past.title: Igniting entrepreneurship, with AIC-RRU
past.text: Monica Gupta led a session for students of the AIC-RRU Incubation Foundation at Rashtriya Raksha University, from idea to MVP and from college to investor exit.
past.alt: Workshop poster: Igniting Entrepreneurship, with Monica Gupta

post.title: Igniting entrepreneurship, with AIC-RRU
post.lede: Monica Gupta led an online session for students of the AIC-RRU Incubation Foundation at Rashtriya Raksha University, on start-up ideas, strategies and success.

p: The session followed the whole journey: from an idea to a minimum viable product, from there to a company that lasts, and from a college project to an investor’s exit.

list: Solve a problem people really have.
Keep building, even when resources are short.
Find mentors, and build a network.
How well you execute counts for more than the idea.

p: To the AIC-RRU Incubation Foundation and Rashtriya Raksha University for the invitation, and to the students for their questions. We run [bootcamps on campus](bootcamps.html) too.

post.close: Want a session for your students?

past.alt: Four people at the Earlyseed Ventures stall

post.title: Our stall at Rotary for Business
post.lede: We took a stall at Rotary for Business, at NESCO in Mumbai, and spent the event in conversation.

p: Rotary brings together people who put service first. It is close to how we see our own work: standing beside founders and businesses that want to create real value.
Health, edtech, fintech, agriculture and defence are among the sectors we have invested in. You can see the companies in [our portfolio](portfolio.html).
If you are an investor who wants to be active, or an industry leader who would like to mentor founders, there are [two ways to join us](invest.html).

post.close: Put your capital or your experience behind a founder.

past.title: International Investors Summit
past.text: The launch of the summit, led by Dr. Anil Sureen in collaboration with us. Monica Gupta moderated the panel, and four companies pitched, including Flying Wedge.
past.alt: Guests applauding a presentation on stage under the summit and Earlyseed Ventures logos

post.title: Launching the International Investors Summit in Dubai
post.lede: In Dubai we marked the launch of the International Investors Summit, an initiative led by Dr. Anil Sureen in collaboration with Earlyseed Ventures.

p: Monica Gupta moderated a five-person panel on how different ecosystems shape the way founders raise money, and what that means for a company’s growth in the long run. It was candid, and drawn from experience.
The keynote looked at strategy: how to build a business that scales across several markets.
Four companies pitched to investors and business collaborators from around the world:
list: SICI, in premium footwear for children

p: This is the start of the collaboration. Its aim is to help capital, conversations and partnerships cross borders.

post.close: Raising across borders, or investing across them?

past.title: India FinTech Forum, IFTA 2025
past.text: The tenth edition of the forum’s awards brought together fintech founders, investors and industry leaders. Sessions covered AI and the fraud stack.
past.alt: Four attendees in front of the IFTA 2025 partner wall

post.title: A decade of fintech, at IFTA 2025
post.lede: We were in Mumbai for IFTA 2025, the India FinTech Forum’s tenth edition, with founders, investors and industry leaders under one roof.

list: How financial services feel to the people using them.
AI, and the next generation of digital-first fintech.

blocks.h: The session that stayed with us
p: A discussion on rethinking the fraud stack in the age of AI: how it is changing fraud detection, risk management and the security of the whole system.
Meeting founders who are pushing at the edges of a sector tells us where it is heading. Our thanks to the India FinTech Forum team for a well-run day.

photos.alt: Three people in front of the India FinTech Forum backdrop
A selfie of three people at the venue

past.title: GITEX Global
past.text: Energy tech, AI, robotics and the circular economy, with talks on climate tech, policy and venture funding.
past.alt: Three visitors among the aircraft on show at GITEX Global

post.title: What we saw at GITEX Global
post.lede: GITEX Global in Dubai is where a great deal of technology meets a great deal of ambition. These are the things that stood out in 2025.

p: A few years ago start-ups had one pavilion. This time there were ten.
Energy tech, AI, robotics and ideas for a circular economy, with talks on climate tech, sustainability, policy and how venture funding is changing.
What impressed us most was who had come. Trade departments, national innovation councils and global funds were there in force, looking for ways to work together.
The best reason for a founder to go is the thinking you bring home: new frameworks, and a clearer sense of where your industry is going.

post.close: The next decade of innovation will be built together.

photos.alt: Crowds beneath a wall of screens listing upcoming GITEX events
